title: AI has its own style in mathematical proving
abstract: arXiv:2611.16527v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large language models increasingly generate mathematical proofs, whether they develop a proving style distinct from that of human mathematicians remains an open question. This question is particularly pressing as mathematicians increasingly voice concerns that proofs generated by large language models are difficult to interpret. Here we ask three large language models to independently reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's \textit{Elements} and compare their citation choices against the human-proof baseline through Jaccard similarity and complex network analysis. We find that AI-generated proofs differ from human proofs, and this difference is stable and reproducible: mean pairwise Jaccard similarity among AI runs (~0.68) is nearly twice that between AI and human proofs (~0.37), and cross-run classification consistency is also high. By examining citation structure in detail, we identify the concrete signature of this difference: app

translated_title: AI在数学证明中拥有自己独特的风格
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型越来越多地生成数学证明，它们是否发展出了一种区别于人类数学家的证明风格仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。随着数学家们日益表达对大语言模型所生成证明难以解读的担忧，这一问题尤为紧迫。在此，我们让三个大语言模型独立地重新证明欧几里得《几何原本》中的全部465个命题，并通过Jaccard相似度和复杂网络分析，将其引用选择与人类证明基线进行比较。我们发现AI生成的证明与人类证明存在差异，而且这种差异是稳定且可复现的：AI各次运行之间的平均成对Jaccard相似度（约0.68）几乎是AI与人类证明之间相似度（约0.37）的两倍，且跨运行的分类一致性也很高。通过详细考察引用结构，我们识别出了这种差异的具体特征……
tldr: 通过让三个大语言模型独立重新证明《几何原本》全部465个命题并与人类证明进行对比分析，研究发现AI生成的数学证明呈现出一种稳定、可复现且明显区别于人类证明的独特风格。
en_tdlr: By having three large language models independently reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's Elements and comparing their citation choices against human proofs, this study finds that AI-generated mathematical proofs exhibit a stable and reproducible style that is distinctly different from human proving.
